title: Packages and repositories
summary: Where apt and dnf get their programs, why a signature is checked, and what dependencies are.

scheme: your machine keeps a copy of the list
jq and what it needs, installed
text: Programs come in packages, stored in repositories.
- apt update only refreshes the list: nothing is installed or upgraded.
- apt install reads that list, downloads the package, and puts its files in place.

scheme: signed with the repository's private key
▼  apt checks it with the public key
├── good signature: the list is used
text: Anyone could run a fake mirror. The signature proves the list comes from the real repository and wasn't changed.
- NO_PUBKEY ("Missing key" on Debian 13): you don't have the key yet. Get it from the project's own website.
- Never switch the check off to make the error go away.
Most packages need others to work: their dependencies. apt and dnf install them for you.
- Libraries (lib…) are code shared by many programs.
- apt remembers why each package is there: manual (you asked for it) or auto (a dependency). apt-mark showmanual and showauto list them.
- apt autoremove removes the auto ones nothing needs anymore.

scheme: install   apt install jq      dnf install jq
text: - apt and dnf talk to repositories and handle dependencies.
- dpkg and rpm work on the packages already on your machine.
- "Which package gave me this file?" is dpkg -S or rpm -qf.
